content.summary: In this reading mission, you will explore an article about how social media affects teenagers today. You will learn to recognize two-sided arguments, locate key facts, and understand linking words that compare opinions.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Connective phrases for balanced arguments: 'On the one hand... On the other hand', 'Moreover / In addition', and 'However / Despite this'
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Key terms related to digital life, such as screen time, cyberbullying, self-esteem, misinformation, and awareness
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Distinguishing between positive and negative arguments by paying attention to transition words

learningObjectives: Understand the main points of an informational text about teenage social media habits.
Identify supporting details, examples, and contrasting viewpoints using linking phrases.
Recognize and interpret connective phrases that show contrast or add information.

contextWarmup.prompt: Read this short comment: 'I love chatting with classmates after school, but sometimes I feel tired after scrolling for hours.' Which linking phrase best introduces the opposite side of using social media?
options: On the other hand
In addition
For example
contextWarmup.explanation: 'On the other hand' introduces a contrasting point or a drawback, which balances the positive side mentioned first.

rules: Use 'On the one hand, ... On the other hand, ...' to present two contrasting sides of an issue fairly.
Use 'Moreover', 'Furthermore', or 'In addition' at the start of a sentence followed by a comma to add a supporting point.
Use 'However' or 'Despite this' to introduce an opposing fact or unexpected limitation.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners often use 'Moreover' when they want to show a contrast, or 'However' when they want to add extra proof. Always check whether your second sentence agrees with the first or shows a different side.
commonTrap.wrong: Social media helps students learn new skills. However, it also allows them to join creative clubs.
commonTrap.correct: Social media helps students learn new skills. In addition, it allows them to join creative clubs.

content.contractionsTitle: Natural Spoken Contractions: Talking About Habits
content.contractionsSubtitle: Observe how subjects and verbs smoothly merge in everyday English:

contractions.subject: It

contractions.exampleContracted: It's difficult to reduce daily screen time.

contractions.exampleFull: They have started an awareness campaign at school.
contractions.exampleContracted: They've started an awareness campaign at school.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns with Contrast Connectives
grammarFormulas.description: Assemble sentence blocks to practice affirmative, negative, and question forms:

items.exampleSentence: Social media has a huge influence on how teenagers see themselves.
items.collocation: have an influence on / strong influence

items.exampleSentence: Cyberbullying is one of the most serious problems that young people face online.
Constantly comparing yourself to others on Instagram can lower your self-esteem.
It is easy to spread misinformation on social media without even realising it.
Experts recommend that teenagers limit their screen time to two hours a day.
items.collocation: limit screen time / excessive screen time

items.exampleSentence: Social media campaigns can raise awareness about important issues like climate change.
Some teenagers buy expensive clothes because of peer pressure on social apps.
items.collocation: succumb to peer pressure / resist peer pressure

items.exampleSentence: Too much time online can cause anxiety and disrupt sleep patterns.
Everything you post online becomes part of your permanent digital footprint.
items.collocation: positive digital footprint / leave a digital footprint

content.passageTitle: Two Sides of the Screen: Teenagers and Social Media
paragraphs: Today, almost every teenager owns a smartphone, and social media platforms are a central part of daily life. Young people use these apps to chat with friends, watch short videos, and share photos. On the one hand, social media helps teenagers build strong friendships across long distances. In addition, it offers creative spaces where young artists and musicians can showcase their work to a wide audience.

Moreover, social networks have become useful tools for learning and social change. Students often join online study groups to prepare for difficult school exams. Furthermore, social campaigns raise awareness about critical topics like mental health and pollution. Many young activists find their voice online, proving that these networks can produce positive real-world changes.

On the other hand, heavy screen time brings clear challenges. Many teenagers spend over five hours a day staring at their phones, which often harms their sleep and physical health. Cyberbullying also remains a dark reality on many platforms. Cruel comments and exclusions can damage a young person's self-esteem and lead to severe anxiety.

However, the issues do not stop there. The rapid spread of misinformation makes it difficult for teenagers to know what is true. Many users also feel intense peer pressure to look perfect in every picture. Despite these serious concerns, experts agree that banning social media completely is not the answer. Instead, teaching healthy digital habits and critical thinking is the best path forward.

drills.instruction: Match each connective phrase with its communicative purpose.

pairs.left: On the one hand... On the other hand
pairs.right: Presents two contrasting perspectives of one topic
Adds an extra supporting point to an argument
Introduces a contrasting fact that follows an existing issue

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the reading passage?
options: To explain both the benefits and the drawbacks of social media for young people
To encourage parents to take smartphones away from all teenagers
To advertise new social media applications for high school students
questions.answer: To explain both the benefits and the drawbacks of social media for young people
questions.explanation: The text explores positive aspects like friendships and study groups, alongside negative aspects like cyberbullying and screen time.

questions.question: According to paragraph 1, how does social media help young artists?
options: It pays them a full-time salary for their artwork.
It gives them a space to display their work to many people.
It buys painting tools and cameras for their projects.
questions.answer: It gives them a space to display their work to many people.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 states that it offers creative spaces where young artists and musicians can showcase their work to a wide audience.

questions.question: What function do words like 'Moreover' and 'Furthermore' serve in paragraph 2?
options: They show that the writer disagrees with the first paragraph.
They introduce extra positive examples that support the argument.
They signal that the passage is ending.
questions.answer: They introduce extra positive examples that support the argument.
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' and 'Furthermore' are transition words of addition that build upon earlier points about learning and social change.

questions.question: According to the passage, how do social media campaigns help the general public?
options: They raise awareness about serious topics such as mental health.
They stop teenagers from doing any homework.
They eliminate all forms of pollution instantly.
questions.answer: They raise awareness about serious topics such as mental health.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 specifically mentions that campaigns raise awareness about critical topics like mental health and pollution.

questions.question: In paragraph 3, which physical problem is linked to spending over five hours a day on phones?
options: Poor sleep habits
Loss of hearing
Broken bones
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 notes that spending over five hours staring at phones often harms sleep and physical health.

questions.question: What psychological effect can cyberbullying and unkind remarks produce in teenagers?
options: It increases their self-esteem and makes them proud.
It damages self-esteem and causes severe anxiety.
It makes them complete their schoolwork faster.
questions.answer: It damages self-esteem and causes severe anxiety.
questions.explanation: The passage states that cruel comments and exclusions can damage a young person's self-esteem and lead to severe anxiety.

questions.question: Why is the presence of misinformation online dangerous for teenagers?
options: It forces teenagers to delete their accounts immediately.
It makes it hard for them to determine what information is true.
It costs them a large amount of money each month.
questions.answer: It makes it hard for them to determine what information is true.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 explains that the rapid spread of misinformation makes it difficult for teenagers to know what is true.

questions.question: Why do some teenagers feel pressure to look perfect in online photos?
options: Because of peer pressure from social media platforms
Because teachers grade their profile photos at school
Because it is required by law in most countries
questions.answer: Because of peer pressure from social media platforms
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 states that many users feel intense peer pressure to look perfect in every picture.

questions.question: What do experts recommend instead of banning social media entirely?
options: Allowing unlimited screen time during school hours
Teaching healthy digital habits and critical thinking
Replacing smartphones with landline telephones
questions.answer: Teaching healthy digital habits and critical thinking
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 concludes that teaching healthy digital habits and critical thinking is the best path forward.

questions.question: Which connective phrase in the final paragraph introduces a conclusion in contrast to the problems mentioned?
options: Despite these serious concerns
In addition to
Because of
questions.explanation: 'Despite these serious concerns' introduces a contrasting judgment: that banning apps is not the answer even though problems exist.

content.summary: In this mission, you will listen to two friends discussing both sides of an argument. Pay close attention to linkers that signal positive and negative points, as well as how words connect together in normal spoken speed.
learningObjectives: Catch the main topic of a debate preparation conversation
Identify supporting points and contrasting arguments in natural speech
Notice how consonant and vowel sounds link together between words

keyPhrases.note: Used at the start of a clause to introduce the first point or advantage.
Used to balance the previous statement with a contrasting reality or disadvantage.
A formal connector used in spoken debates to introduce additional evidence.
Refers to effects or results that will become obvious over an extended period.

connectedSpeech.note: The preposition 'on' weakens to an unstressed schwa sound in rapid speech.
Consonant-to-vowel linking connects the ending 's' of 'helps' smoothly to 'us'.
The word 'of' is reduced to an unstressed schwa sound before the consonant.
The sound at the end of 'teach' blends directly into the start of 'young'.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Balancing Arguments on Social Media

content.summary: Learn how to write balanced opinion paragraphs about social media using formal linking words. You will practice presenting both positive and negative points clearly and supporting your claims with reasons.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Balance Two Sides of an Argument
blueprintItems.formula: On the one hand, [positive point]. On the other hand, [negative point].
blueprintItems.example: On the one hand, social media helps teenagers make friends online. On the other hand, it can take away valuable study time.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Add Supporting Points
blueprintItems.formula: [First argument]. Moreover / In addition / Furthermore, [additional argument].
blueprintItems.example: Online platforms let students share study notes quickly. Moreover, they give young creators an audience for their art.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Introduce a Direct Contrast
blueprintItems.formula: [First statement]. However / Nevertheless / Despite this, [contrasting statement].
blueprintItems.example: Many apps offer educational videos for teenagers. However, excessive screen time can cause sleep problems.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always place a comma immediately after transitional linking words at the start of a sentence.
mechanicsRules.badExample: However teenagers spend too much time on their phones.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: However, teenagers spend too much time on their phones.
mechanicsRules.why: Words like 'However', 'Moreover', and 'Furthermore' are sentence connectors and require a pause in writing.

mechanicsRules.rule: Do not join two independent sentences with only a comma. Use a full stop or a semicolon before a linking word.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Social media is fun, however it can distract students from homework.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Social media is fun. However, it can distract students from homework.
mechanicsRules.why: This error is called a comma splice. 'However' is an adverb, not a coordinating conjunction like 'but'.

mechanicsRules.rule: Follow 'Despite this' with a comma and a complete clause containing a subject and a verb.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Despite this spending five hours online every day.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Despite this, many teenagers still manage to finish their school projects on time.
mechanicsRules.why: 'Despite this' functions as a prepositional phrase showing contrast, so it must introduce a full sentence.

sampleSentences.en: On the one hand, photo-sharing apps encourage artistic hobbies. On the other hand, they can cause unhealthy social comparison.
sampleSentences.id: Di satu sisi, aplikasi berbagi foto mendorong hobi artistik. Di sisi lain, aplikasi tersebut dapat menyebabkan perbandingan sosial yang tidak sehat.
sampleSentences.focus: Using 'On the one hand' and 'On the other hand' to balance two viewpoints

sampleSentences.focus: Using 'Despite this' to show an unexpected contrast

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Balance the Pros and Cons of Messaging Apps
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three sentences about messaging apps like WhatsApp or Instagram. Use 'On the one hand' for a positive aspect, 'On the other hand' for a disadvantage, and 'Moreover' to add an extra supporting detail.
guidedLabChallenges.example: On the one hand, messaging apps make group projects much easier to organize. On the other hand, late-night messages can harm sleep quality. Moreover, constant alerts make it hard to focus on homework.
guidedLabChallenges.placeholder: Write your three sentences here using the target linkers...

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Express Contrast on Screen Time
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three sentences about daily smartphone use. State one benefit, introduce a drawback using 'However,', and finish with a concluding thought using 'Despite this,'.
guidedLabChallenges.example: Smartphones allow teens to access news articles within seconds. However, spending several hours scrolling can cause eye strain. Despite this, many students rely on mobile devices for schoolwork every day.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the two sentences into one pair using 'On the one hand,' and 'On the other hand,':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Social media lets teens express their ideas. It exposes them to negative feedback.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start the first sentence with 'On the one hand,' and the second with 'On the other hand,'.
targetAnswers: On the one hand, social media lets teens express their ideas. On the other hand, it exposes them to negative feedback.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use 'On the one hand,' before the first point and 'On the other hand,' before the second point to balance both sides.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine these two sentences by inserting 'Moreover,' at the beginning of the second sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Video blogs teach teenagers practical cooking skills. They inspire young people to try new recipes.
practicumQuestions.hint: Keep the first sentence unchanged. Begin the second sentence with 'Moreover,' followed by a comma.
targetAnswers: Video blogs teach teenagers practical cooking skills. Moreover, they inspire young people to try new recipes.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Moreover,' is placed at the start of the second sentence followed by a comma to add a supporting point.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the punctuation and capitalization in the following sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: however spending too much time online causes fatigue
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first word, add a comma after 'However', and end with a period.
targetAnswers: However, spending too much time online causes fatigue.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Transitional adverbs like 'However' must be capitalized at the start of a sentence and followed by a comma.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Connect these two statements using 'In addition,' to introduce the second sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Online forums connect people with rare hobbies. They give members a safe space to ask questions.
practicumQuestions.hint: Write two complete sentences. Start the second sentence with 'In addition,'.
targetAnswers: Online forums connect people with rare hobbies. In addition, they give members a safe space to ask questions.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'In addition,' introduces an extra positive fact that reinforces the previous idea.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite this sentence pair by replacing 'But' with 'However,':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Many apps offer educational games. But they also display distracting advertisements.
practicumQuestions.hint: Replace 'But' with 'However,' and maintain correct capitalization.
targetAnswers: Many apps offer educational games. However, they also display distracting advertisements.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In formal B1 writing, 'However,' followed by a comma is preferred over starting a sentence with 'But'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the comma splice in this sentence by separating it into two sentences with correct punctuation:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Social media helps students collaborate, furthermore it improves their communication skills.
practicumQuestions.hint: Place a period before 'Furthermore' and a comma after it.
targetAnswers: Social media helps students collaborate. Furthermore, it improves their communication skills.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Furthermore' cannot join two main clauses with only a comma. You must use a period to create two sentences.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine these two contrasting facts using 'Despite this,' at the start of the second sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Doctors recommend limiting screen time to two hours daily. Most teenagers spend over four hours on their phones.
practicumQuestions.hint: Begin the second sentence with 'Despite this,' followed by a comma.
targetAnswers: Doctors recommend limiting screen time to two hours daily. Despite this, most teenagers spend over four hours on their phones.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Despite this,' signals an unexpected result or contrasting reality to the fact mentioned before.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the capitalization and punctuation in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: on the one hand teenagers enjoy instant messaging
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize 'On', place a comma after 'hand', and end with a full stop.
targetAnswers: On the one hand, teenagers enjoy instant messaging.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'On the one hand' requires a capital 'O' at the start of a sentence and a comma after 'hand'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the following sentence by changing 'Although online communities are fun, they carry risks.' into two sentences using 'Nevertheless,':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Although online communities are fun, they carry risks.
practicumQuestions.hint: Write 'Online communities are fun. Nevertheless, they carry risks.'
targetAnswers: Online communities are fun. Nevertheless, they carry risks.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Nevertheless,' acts as a transition word between two independent sentences to show contrast.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the second sentence by adding a reason why social media can cause stress, beginning with 'However,':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Social media makes it easy to follow celebrity news. [Write a contrasting sentence about online pressure using 'However,']
practicumQuestions.hint: Example: 'However, comparing your life to celebrities can cause stress.'
targetAnswers: However, comparing your life to celebrities can cause stress.
However, it can make teenagers feel insecure about their own lives.
However, seeing perfect photos online can make young people feel unhappy.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A good contrast sentence addresses the negative side of following celebrities online using 'However,'.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Social Media and Young People

content.summary: Practise giving a clear opinion about how social media affects young people. Use connective phrases such as “firstly,” “however,” “because of this,” and “in conclusion” to organise both sides of your argument.
content.audioGuidance: Speak at a steady pace and pause briefly between your main points. Make your voice fall at the end of a complete statement. Use a rising tone when you are asking a yes-or-no question. Pronounce each syllable clearly, especially in longer words such as “misinformation” and “awareness.”

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.explanation: Keep vowel sounds clear in words such as “screen,” “time,” and “influence.” Do not rush through the middle of longer words.

pillars.name: Word Stress
pillars.explanation: Give one syllable in each longer word more force. For example, the main stress in “misinformation” is on “MA,” and the main stress in “awareness” is on “WARE.”

pillars.name: Connected Speech
pillars.explanation: Join the final sound of one word to the next when it feels natural, as in “spend time online.” Keep the words understandable.

pillars.name: Argument Structure
pillars.target: Make your opinion easy to follow
pillars.explanation: State your view, give a reason or example, and then add another side with “however” or “on the other hand.” Finish with a short conclusion.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: “Influence” has its main stress on the first syllable. In “self-esteem,” both parts receive clear stress.
“Cyberbullying” starts with a strong first syllable. In “misinformation,” the main stress is on “MA.”
Stress the first word in “screen time.” In “awareness,” the strongest syllable is “WARE.”
Give the first syllable of “social” and “media” clear stress. In “compare,” stress the second syllable.

drills.targetText: Social media can influence how young people see themselves.
drills.phonetic: /ˈsəʊʃəl ˈmiːdiə kən ˈɪnfluəns haʊ jʌŋ ˈpiːpəl siː ðəmˈselvz/
drills.hint: Make the first syllables in “social” and “influence” clear.

drills.targetText: However, cyberbullying can lower a teenager’s self-esteem.
drills.phonetic: /haʊˈevə ˈsaɪbəˌbʊliɪŋ kən ˈləʊər ə ˈtiːneɪdʒəz ˌselfɪˈstiːm/
drills.focus: Stress in key vocabulary and a pause after “however”
drills.hint: Pause briefly after “however,” then give “cyberbullying” and “self-esteem” clear stress.

drills.targetText: On the other hand, some posts spread misinformation.
drills.phonetic: /ɒn ði ˈʌðə hænd sʌm pəʊsts spred ˌmɪsɪnfəˈmeɪʃən/
drills.focus: Connective phrases and the stress in “misinformation”
drills.hint: Pause after “on the other hand.” Stress the “MA” sound in “misinformation.”

drills.targetText: In conclusion, young people should limit their screen time.
drills.phonetic: /ɪn kənˈkluːʒən jʌŋ ˈpiːpəl ʃəd ˈlɪmɪt ðeə skriːn taɪm/
drills.focus: Clear final consonants and falling intonation
drills.hint: Say “in conclusion” clearly, then let your voice fall at the end of the sentence.

roleplay.context: You and a classmate are preparing a short classroom discussion about the effects of social media on teenagers. Take turns sharing benefits and problems, and support your ideas with reasons.

turns.speaker: Classmate
turns.text: Do you think social media has a positive influence on young people?
turns.translation: Apakah menurutmu media sosial memiliki pengaruh positif terhadap anak muda?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: In some ways, yes. For example, it can help teenagers raise awareness about important issues.
turns.translation: Dalam beberapa hal, ya. Misalnya, media sosial dapat membantu remaja meningkatkan kesadaran tentang isu-isu penting.

turns.speaker: Classmate
turns.text: That is true. However, what problems should teenagers be careful about?
turns.translation: Itu benar. Namun, masalah apa yang perlu diwaspadai oleh remaja?

turns.speaker: Student
turns.text: They should watch out for cyberbullying and misinformation, and try to limit their screen time.
turns.translation: Mereka harus waspada terhadap perundungan siber dan misinformasi, serta berusaha membatasi waktu layar.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 20 seconds about a time social media helped you or someone you know.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell me about a useful or positive experience with social media.
storyPoints: Which platform or feature you used
How it helped you or someone you know
Why you think this experience was positive
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Social media helped me find useful information, and I shared it with my friends.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈsəʊʃəl ˈmiːdiə helpt miː faɪnd ˈjuːsfəl ˌɪnfəˈmeɪʃən/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Tell a short story in a clear order. Use past tense for what happened and give a reason for your opinion.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 20 seconds about a problem young people can face on social media.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe a social media problem and explain what young people can do about it.
storyPoints: Name a problem, such as cyberbullying or misinformation
Explain how it can affect a young person
Suggest one way to respond or stay safe
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Cyberbullying can hurt a teenager’s self-esteem, so they should tell someone they trust.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Explain the problem, its effect, and your suggestion. Use “so” or “because” to connect your ideas.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to your classmate and give your view with one supporting reason.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your classmate asks whether social media is useful for learning. Answer and explain your opinion.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are discussing social media and learning with a classmate before a classroom debate.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a student who must give an opinion and support it with a reason.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I think social media can help with learning because people can share useful information.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ θɪŋk ˈsəʊʃəl ˈmiːdiə kən help wɪð ˈlɜːnɪŋ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Answer the question directly, then use “because” to give a reason.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to your classmate with a contrast and a supporting example.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your classmate says social media is always good for teenagers. Politely explain one possible problem.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: Your classmate has given a very positive view of social media during a school discussion.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a student who should disagree politely and explain one concern.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I understand your point. However, too much screen time can affect sleep.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ ˌʌndəˈstænd jɔː pɔɪnt haʊˈevə tuː mʌtʃ skriːn taɪm kən əˈfekt sliːp/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Show that you have listened, then use “however” to introduce a different point.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Give your classmate one practical suggestion and explain why it may help.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your friend says they spend too much time on their phone. What do you suggest?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A friend asks for advice because they feel they spend too much time scrolling social media.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a supportive friend who gives a simple, realistic suggestion.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: You could set a daily screen time limit so you have more time to rest.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /juː kəd set ə ˈdeɪli skriːn taɪm ˈlɪmɪt səʊ juː hæv mɔː taɪm tə rest/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use “you could” to make a polite suggestion and “so” to explain its result.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Explain how a young person can check whether an online claim is reliable.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your classmate has seen a surprising post online. Tell them what they should do before sharing it.
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You and a classmate are talking about a surprising claim that appeared on social media.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a student who explains how to avoid spreading misinformation.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: They should check the source first because the post may contain misinformation.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðeɪ ʃəd tʃek ðə sɔːs fɜːst bɪˈkɒz ðə pəʊst meɪ kənˈteɪn ˌmɪsɪnfəˈmeɪʃən/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Give a clear piece of advice and connect it to a reason with “because.”

practicumQuestions.instruction: Use at least three target words to explain one benefit and one problem of social media.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Speak for 20 seconds. Use words such as “influence,” “self-esteem,” “awareness,” “screen time,” or “misinformation.”
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Social media can raise awareness, but misinformation can have a negative influence on young people.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈsəʊʃəl ˈmiːdiə kən reɪz əˈweənəs bət ˌmɪsɪnfəˈmeɪʃən kən hæv ə ˈneɡətɪv ˈɪnfluəns/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Choose words that fit your meaning and use them in complete sentences.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Give an argument with one benefit and one contrasting problem. Use “because” and “however.”
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Complete this idea in your own words: “Social media is useful because ____. However, ____.”
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Social media is useful because it helps people share ideas. However, users should check their screen time.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈsəʊʃəl ˈmiːdiə ɪz ˈjuːsfəl bɪˈkɒz ɪt helps ˈpiːpəl ʃeər aɪˈdɪəz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use “because” to give a reason and “however” to introduce a contrasting point.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say “misinformation,” “awareness,” and “influence” clearly, then use each word in a short sentence.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Listen to the words and repeat them, stressing the correct syllable.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Misinformation spreads quickly, and media can influence public awareness.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In “misinformation,” stress “MA.” In “awareness,” stress “WARE.” In “influence,” stress the first syllable.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Ask the question with a rising tone, then say the opinion with a falling tone.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say, “Can social media help young people?” Then say, “It can help them share useful information.”
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Can social media help young people? It can help them share useful information.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /kən ˈsəʊʃəl ˈmiːdiə help jʌŋ ˈpiːpəl | ɪt kən help ðəm ʃeə ˈjuːsfəl ˌɪnfəˈmeɪʃən/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Let your voice rise slightly at the end of the yes-or-no question. Let it fall at the end of the statement.
